Colorbee Help

Menus

Every command in Colorbee's menus, with its shortcut and what it does.

Shortcuts shown are the defaults. You can change them in Colorbee ▸ Settings ▸ Shortcuts.

Colorbee · File · Edit · View · Image · Layer · Page · Adjustments · Effects · Redact · Window · Help

Colorbee

CommandShortcutWhat it does
About ColorbeeVersion and credits.
Settings…⌘,Appearance, PDF resolution, keyboard shortcuts and export presets.
ServicesOther apps' services, provided by macOS.
Hide Colorbee⌘HHide Colorbee's windows until you switch back.
Hide Others⌥⌘HHide every other app's windows.
Show AllShow every app's windows again.
Quit Colorbee⌘QQuit Colorbee. Your work is saved automatically.

File

CommandShortcutWhat it does
New⌘NStart a new blank 1920 × 1080 image.
Paste into New Image⇧⌘VOpen the clipboard image as a new document at its own size.
Open…⌘OOpen an image (PNG, JPEG, HEIC, TIFF, GIF, BMP or WebP) or a Colorbee project.
Open RecentOpen an image or project you opened recently. Clear Menu forgets the list.
Close⌘WClose this window.
Save⌘SSave the image. Untitled images ask for a name and format.
Save As…⇧⌘SSave a copy under a new name or in another format.
DuplicateOpen a copy of this image in a new window.
Revert To SavedThrow away changes since the last save.
Export…⌥⌘SSave a copy in any format, with a quality setting for JPEG and HEIC.
Export as PDF…Save every page as a PDF, in order. Pixels only: no text under a redaction, and no details about who made it.
Export AsSave a PNG at a common size, such as Slack (760 px). Edit the sizes in Settings ▸ Export Presets.
Share…Send the image with AirDrop, Messages, Mail and more.
Set as Desktop PictureUse the image as your desktop picture.
Page Setup…⇧⌘PChoose the paper size and orientation for printing.
Print…⌘PPrint the image, scaled to fit the page.

Edit

CommandShortcutWhat it does
Undo⌘ZUndo the last change.
Redo⇧⌘ZRedo the change you just undid.
Undo on Active Layer⌥⌘ZUndo the active layer's last change only, leaving later changes on other layers in place.
New Snapshot…Name the image as it is now, so you can go back to it from the History panel.
Cut⌘XCopy the selection to the clipboard, then clear it.
Copy⌘CCopy the selection (or the whole image) to the clipboard as a PNG.
Copy Merged⇧⌘CCopy the selection as all visible layers show it together.
Copy Text⌥⌘CCopy the text in the selection, or the whole page, as plain text. Read on this Mac.
Paste⌘VPaste an image as a selection you can move and resize.
Paste in Place⌥⇧⌘VPaste exactly where the copied pixels came from, in this image or another one.
DeleteClear the selected pixels to Color 2 (or transparency).
Select All⌘ASelect the whole image.
Deselect⌘DRemove the selection, placing any moved pixels.
Invert Selection⇧⌘ISelect everything that isn't selected, and nothing that is.
Feather…Soften the selection's edge, so changes fade out across it.
Modify Selection ▸ Expand…Grow the selection outward by a number of pixels.
Modify Selection ▸ Contract…Shrink the selection inward by a number of pixels.
Modify Selection ▸ Smooth…Round off the selection's ragged edges and remove stray specks.
Select SubjectSelect the main subject of a photo, found on this Mac. With several, click the one you want.
Color Range…Select the colors you click in the picture, and colors near them.
Luminance Range…Select by brightness: the shadows, midtones or highlights.
Graduated SelectionDrag a line: fully selected where it starts, fading to nothing where it ends.

View

CommandShortcutWhat it does
Zoom In⌘=Zoom in one step.
Zoom Out⌘-Zoom out one step.
Actual Size⌘0Show the image at 100%, one image pixel per screen point.
Zoom to Fit⌘9Fit the whole image in the window.
Pixel Grid⌘'Show a line between pixels at 400% zoom and above.
Rulers⌘RShow or hide pixel rulers along the canvas.
Before/After⌥⌘BCompare the image now with how it was opened or last saved.
Sidebar⌃⌘SShow or hide the whole sidebar on the right, with the panels you last had open.
Layers⌘LShow or hide the Layers panel.
AdjustmentsShow or hide the Adjustments panel, where an adjustment layer's settings live.
History⌘YShow or hide every step you've taken, to jump back to any of them.
Clipboard History⌥⌘VShow or hide the last 10 images you copied or pasted.
Info⌥⌘IShow or hide the image's details: file, size, color profile and how the photo was taken.
Page Sidebar⌥⌘2Show or hide the pages, down the left side.
Status BarShow or hide the bar along the bottom of the window.
Enter Full Screen⌃⌘FFill the screen with this window.

Image

CommandShortcutWhat it does
Crop to Selection⇧⌘XTrim the image to the selection's edges.
Crop…Crop with a box you drag: free, a set shape, or an exact pixel size.
Resize and Skew…⌘EChange the size of the selection (or whole image) by percent or pixels, or slant it.
Canvas Properties…⌥⌘EChange the canvas size or make its background transparent.
Rotate ▸ 90° Clockwise, 90° Counter-Clockwise, 180°Turn or mirror the selection, or the whole image if nothing is selected.
Flip ▸ Horizontal, VerticalTurn or mirror the selection, or the whole image if nothing is selected.
Straighten…Turn the image a little to level a horizon or a crooked scan.
Perspective Correction…Square up a photo of a whiteboard, a document or a building.
Remove BackgroundMake everything but the photo's subject transparent, with soft edges. Found on this Mac; nothing is uploaded.
Symmetry ▸ Off, Vertical, Horizontal, BothMirror pencil, brush and eraser strokes across the image's center lines.

Layer

CommandShortcutWhat it does
New Layer⇧⌘NAdd a transparent layer above the active one.
Duplicate Layer⌘JCopy the active layer (or every chosen layer), with its settings, just above it.
Delete Layer⌘⌫Delete the active layer, or every chosen layer. The only layer, or a locked one, can't be deleted.
Lift Subject to New LayerCopy the photo's subject onto a new layer, leaving this one as it is.
Merge Down⇧⌘ECombine the active layer into the one below, or the chosen layers into one, keeping how they look.
Merge Visible⌥⇧⌘ECombine every visible layer into one. Hidden layers stay.
FlattenCombine all visible layers into one and drop hidden layers.
New Adjustment Layer ▸ Hue/Saturation, Levels, Auto Contrast, Curves, Desaturate, Sepia, Posterize, Invert, Gaussian Blur, Sharpen, Adjust PhotoAdd an adjustment layer: it changes how the layers below look, without changing their pixels.
Merge AdjustmentMerge the active adjustment layer and the layers below it into one layer, keeping the look.
Revert LayerPut the active layer's pixels back as they were at the last save.
Hide LayerHide or show the active layer, or every chosen layer.
Lock LayerLock the active layer (or every chosen layer) against changes, or unlock it.
Layer Properties…Rename the active layer and change its blend mode and opacity.

Page

CommandShortcutWhat it does
New PageAdd a blank page after this one, the same size, filled with Color 2.
Duplicate PageCopy this page, with its layers, just after it.
Delete PageRemove this page from the document.
Move Page UpMove this page one place earlier.
Move Page DownMove this page one place later.
Previous Page⌥⌘↑Show the page before this one.
Next Page⌥⌘↓Show the page after this one.

Adjustments

CommandShortcutWhat it does
Adjust Photo…Exposure, light, color and detail sliders, Auto, and filters, in a panel at the side.
Adjust Photo: Same as LastApply the Adjust Photo settings you last used again, to the selection or layer.
Copy Photo SettingsCopy the active Adjust Photo layer's settings, to paste onto another picture.
Paste Photo SettingsOpen Adjust Photo with the copied settings, or give them to the active Adjust Photo layer.
Paste Photo Settings as Adjustment LayerAdd an Adjust Photo layer with the copied settings.
Auto ContrastStretch the darkest pixels to black and the lightest to white, in one step.
Levels…Set the black point, white point and midtones, with a histogram. Auto sets them from the image.
Curves…Reshape the tones with a curve, for all colors together or one at a time.
Hue/Saturation…Shift colors around the color wheel, or make them more or less vivid.
Desaturate⇧⌘UTurn the selection or image to grayscale.
Sepia…Give the selection or image warm brown tones.
Invert Colors⌘ITurn colors into their opposites (black becomes white).
Posterize…Reduce each color channel to a few levels, for a flat poster look.
Remove Red-EyeTurn red pupils from a flash dark. With a selection, fixes the red inside it. On this Mac.
New Adjustment Layer ▸ Hue/Saturation, Levels, Auto Contrast, Curves, Desaturate, Sepia, Posterize, Invert, Gaussian Blur, Sharpen, Adjust PhotoAdd an adjustment layer: it changes how the layers below look, without changing their pixels.

Effects

CommandShortcutWhat it does
Gaussian Blur…Blur the selection (or image). Each separate selected area is blurred on its own.
Motion Blur…Streak the selection or image along an angle, as if it moved.
Sharpen…Make edges crisper.
Pixelate…Turn the selection (or image) into large square blocks.
Add Noise…Add grain, in color or monochrome.
Emboss…Turn the selection or image into a gray relief.
Vignette…Darken (or lighten) toward the edges of the selection or image.
Spotlight…Dim, blur or desaturate everything outside the selection. Select the area to keep first.
Drop Shadow…A soft shadow behind the image or the selected object, following its shape. The canvas grows to fit.
Border…An outline around the image or the selected object, following its shape. The canvas grows to fit.

Redact

CommandShortcutWhat it does
Auto-Redact…Find emails, phone numbers, keys and more on this Mac, then hide the ones you choose.
Blur…Blur every selected area, each on its own, as one step.
Pixelate…Pixelate every selected area, each on its own, as one step.
Solid Fill with Color 1Cover every selected area with Color 1. The most secure way to hide text.

Window

CommandShortcutWhat it does
Minimize⌘MMinimize this window to the Dock.
ZoomMake this window as large as it needs to be.
Bring All to FrontBring all Colorbee windows to the front.
